slides.title: Deciding Which Congresses Matter
bullets: Decides in advance which congresses to attend, with what objectives
Sets resources per congress and its connection to the plan's other levers
An earlier module covered excellent execution of a single congress
This lesson places that execution inside the annual strategic plan

slides.title: Mapping and Evaluating Every Event
bullets: Map the full calendar: international, regional, and niche specialist events
Evaluate each by expected presence of priority KOLs and DOLs
Also weigh the likelihood of relevant own or competitor data, and cost versus value

slides.title: Three Tiers of Congress Investment
bullets: Strategic presence: posters, own presentations, satellite symposia, broad team
Coverage: lighter presence focused on intelligence and selective KOL contact
Remote monitoring: no physical presence, but publications are still tracked

slides.title: Congress Plan Meets Publications and Stakeholders
bullets: Aligns with the publication plan so own data appears at the right congress
Aligns with stakeholder strategy so priority KOLs get coherent attention
Assigns clear responsibilities for preparation, execution, and follow-up

slides.title: From Isolated Events to a Coherent Sequence
bullets: Congress activity stops being a series of disconnected annual events
Each congress gets a clear purpose tied to the plan's strategic imperatives
Medical return becomes something you can evaluate and improve every cycle

takeaway.title: The congress plan turns a year of events into a coordinated strategic sequence
bullets: Not every congress deserves the same level of investment
Investment tier depends on KOL presence, data likelihood, and cost versus value
It must stay coordinated with the publication plan and stakeholder strategy
